name: Treaty with the Omaha, 1865
promises: Article 1: the Omaha ceded the northern part of their reservation; Royce records it was for locating the Winnebago (Royce p. 834).
Article 2: the United States to pay $50,000 on ratification, spent by the agent on goods, provisions, stock, buildings, tools and improvements on the reservation.
Article 3: Article 8 of the 1854 treaty extended for ten years, and $7,000 paid for damage from the Winnebago's temporary stay and timber use on Omaha land.
Article 4: the remaining reservation to be allotted in severalty, and whites not to go or reside on it.

breaches.what: The Supreme Court held that the United States did not comply with Article 2 when it bought 103 stock cattle with Omaha money in 1867 and 50 died from bad condition, and upheld $1,666.50 for them. It also upheld $3,127.08 of Omaha money spent in 1875 on an infirmary unfit for their use, a misappropriation under the 1854 and 1865 treaties.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Supreme Court, United States v. Omaha Tribe of Indians, 253 U.S. 275 (1920), affirming on these items the Court of Claims, Omaha Tribe of Indians v. United States, 53 Ct. Cl. 549 (1918), findings VIII and IX, under the jurisdictional act of June 22, 1910

source.title: United States v. Omaha Tribe of Indians, 253 U.S. 275 (June 1, 1920)

breaches.quote: In either event the fault lay with the agents of the United States

breaches.what: The Omaha claimed fair compensation for the land ceded in 1865 for the Winnebago (Docket 225-B). The claim was never tried; it was settled together with the tribe's other claims in Docket 225 Consolidated by a compromise the Commission approved.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Indian Claims Commission, Omaha Tribe of Nebraska v. United States, Docket 225-B, settled in Docket 225 Consolidated (February 11, 1960)

source.title: Omaha Tribe of Nebraska et al. v. United States, Dockets 225-A to 225-D, Findings of Fact on Proposed Compromise Settlement (February 11, 1960), 8 Ind. Cl. Comm. 392

compensation: The treaty price was $50,000 (Article 2) plus $7,000 in damages (Article 3). The Court of Claims allowed $1,666.50 for the dead cattle and $3,127.08 for the infirmary as part of a 1918 judgment of $122,295.31 on several Omaha treaty claims; the Supreme Court in 1920 upheld those two items and struck $4,560 for horses. The Docket 225-B claim for the land was later settled, not decided.
today: The Docket 225-B claim for fair payment for the ceded land was settled, not decided, as part of the 1960 Docket 225 Consolidated compromise.

openQuestions: The settlement total for Docket 225 Consolidated and the acreage in Docket 225-B are poorly scanned; neither is recorded.
Royce (p. 837) records 20 more sections bought from the Omaha by Act of June 22, 1874 for the Winnebago; that is a separate event.
The Omaha Tribe's own account of the 1865 cession was not located in this pass.

plain.promised: The Omaha sold the northern part of their reservation, for the Winnebago, for $50,000 in goods, cattle and improvements and $7,000 in damages, and kept the rest as allotted land closed to whites.
plain.happened: The Supreme Court held in 1920 that the United States failed the treaty when it bought sick cattle with Omaha money, half of which died, and spent Omaha money on an unusable infirmary.
plain.today: The courts allowed $1,666.50 for the cattle and $3,127.08 for the infirmary. A later claim that the land itself was underpaid was settled in 1960, not decided.
